issues.description: The problem statement (lines 40-41) refers to a method named get_total_number_of_students() using snake_case, whereas the UML, template comments, and the solution use the camelCase name getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This inconsistent method naming in the problem text can confuse students about the exact method name/signature they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name in the problem statement to camelCase (getTotalNumberOfStudents) to match the UML, template comments, and solution. Alternatively, explicitly state that students should implement getTotalNumberOfStudents() (camelCase) and treat any snake_case mention as a typo.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the total-students method using snake_case as get_total_number_of_students(), while the UML and the Java solution use the Java-conventional camelCase getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This inconsistent identifier naming for the same concept (total number of students) across artifacts can confuse students about the exact method name they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent method name across all artifacts. Prefer Java convention: replace get_total_number_of_students() in the problem statement with getTotalNumberOfStudents(), so the problem text, UML, template instructions, and solution all reference the same camelCase method name.
